subject: Film & Cinema
title: Slapstick: Physical Comedy's Roots
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Slapstick: Physical Comedy's Roots.

hook.text: A pie hits a face. A man slips on a banana peel. The audience roars.

buildup.text: Slapstick dates back to silent film — Chaplin, Keaton, and Lloyd built careers on falls.

discovery.text: Physical comedy transcends language, which is why it dominated the silent era.

twist.text: What looks effortless on screen requires incredible athletic skill and precise timing.

climax.text: Slapstick lives on in Jackie Chan, Jim Carrey, and countless internet videos.

punchline.text: Falling down is the oldest art form.

quiz.question: Why was slapstick ideal for silent films?
options: Physical comedy needs no dialogue or language
